messages:
mara: heads-up, started seeing a spike in east-west packet drops on g7gn clusters in use1 around 10:40 UTC. pod-to-pod p99 latency jumped, and we see RX/TX error counters incrementing on the NICs. dmesg shows `eth0: rx checksum failed` and `NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0 (mlx5_core): transmit queue 0 timed out`

samir: ugh. did we roll any fw or kernel last night?

mara: we did a staged nic fw bump (mlx5 2.3.1 -> 2.3.3) on ~15% of fleet last night as part of the firmware cadence. but errors show up on both fw versions — starting to suspect offload interaction + jumbo frames.

jon: can you paste `ethtool -k eth0` + a short `ethtool -S eth0 | egrep -i "rx|tx|err|drop"`?

mara: snippets below (redacted host ids):

```
# ethtool -k eth0
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: on
large-receive-offload: on
```

```
# ethtool -S eth0 | egrep -i "rx|tx|err|drop"
rx_packets: 12452345
rx_errors: 42
rx_crc_errors: 0
rx_missed: 0
tx_packets: 13011234
tx_errors: 15
rx_drop: 37
tx_drop: 3
```

mara: counters are small but climb correlated with observed pod stalls.

samir: if GRO/LRO or GSO behaves oddly with certain MTU/segmentation patterns we can get checksum failures surfaced by the stack. what MTU are these hosts on?

mara: default 9000 on the cluster (we use jumbo frames).

jon: two quick canaries to try: (1) disable GRO/LRO on a canary node, (2) try forcing `ethtool -K eth0 rx off gso off gro off tso off` and see if errors stop. also test with MTU 1500 on one node to rule out jumbo interaction.

lisa: infra-bot just flagged a control-plane fw rollout to the same AZ at 03:00 UTC — could be unrelated but worth noting.

infra-bot: deployment: nic-fw/2.3.3 -> started rollout to use1b at 03:00 UTC by fw-team (canary 10% -> 100%). no rollback events recorded.

mara: rolling `ethtool -K` change now on a single canary host.

(5m later)

mara: canary node after disabling offloads: rx_errors=0, rx_drop stabilized, pod p99 latency back to baseline.

samir: good sign — points to offload path. jon, could this be a driver regression with large MTU + GSO/GRO + RDMA enabled?

jon: possible. mlx5 driver has known corner cases when RoCE is enabled and TSO/GSO interacts with the NIC's checksum handling. if RDMA/rocev2 is enabled and the NIC firmware expects different header alignment, jumbo frames + GSO can trigger checksums to be mis-validated.

lisa: how widespread is this? can we identify hosts with both RDMA enabled and jumbo MTU?

mara: running a query now: `aws-catalog` tag + `rdma_enabled=true` + MTU=9000 -> ~420 hosts across use1 (mix of g7gn and g6gn).

samir: mitigation plan suggestion: 1) rollback any risky fw rollouts in the affected AZs (pause further rollouts), 2) push a temporary cluster-level sysctl/ethtool change to disable GRO/GSO on affected hosts, 3) schedule a coordinated fw + driver test with mlx5 upstream, 4) prepare a canary that switches MTU to 1500 for a subset to compare.

jon: actionable commands for ops:
```
# disable offloads
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off
# verify
ethtool -k eth0 | egrep -i "gro|gso|tso"
# if using rdma, confirm ib devices
ibv_devinfo || true
# temporary mtu change
sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1500
```

mara: applied ethtool change via orchestration to 10 canaries across AZs. monitoring.

(10m later)

mara: canaries look stable. filing ops-ticket with aggregated counters/logs and starting pause on fw rollout.

samir: please also add a healthcheck to block autoscaling onto hosts with rdma=true + mtu=9000 until we get a permanent fix.

jon: I'll open an upstream bug with driver/firmware folks including packet captures and ethtool dumps. we should test a kernel from the nextstable branch and also test firmware 2.3.2 vs 2.3.3 matrix.

lisa: cc: fw-team and networking. good triage — if disabling offloads fixes it, we can keep that as a short-term cluster flag while we validate a true driver/firmware fix.

mara: filing postmortem stub and linking ticket: OPS-7241. will update with timelines and rollout pause details.

infra-bot: ticket OPS-7241 created by mara. severity: S2. labels: networking, firmware, canary-mitigation.

samir: thanks — let's sync in 30 for next steps. :thumbsup:
